On March 31st, 1990 Mike Weaver fought John Tate at the Stokley Athletics Center in Knoxville in a 15 round bout for the WBA World heavyweight title that ended by knockout in the 15th round securing the victory for Weaver.

On February 18th, 1995 Montell Griffin faced James Toney for the first time at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas for the IBF Inter-continental Light Heavyweight title with the bout ending with a majority decision win for Griffin.

On December 6th, 1996 Montell Griffin and James Toney fought for a second time at the Lawlor Events Center in Reno for World Light Heavyweight titles resulting in an unanimous decision win for Griffin.

On November 14th, 1966 Muhammad Ali faced Cleveland Williams at the Astrodome in Houston, TX. They fought for WBC World Heavyweight titles in what was supposed to be a 15 round bout only went 3 resulting in a win for Ali.

On February 6th, 1967 Muhammad Ali fought Ernie Terrel at the Astrodome in Hourston, Tx. They fought for WBA and WBC World Heavyweight titles in a bout that went 15 rounds ending in a unanimous decision victory for Ali.

On September 20th, 1972 Muhammad Ali faced Floyd Patterson for a second time at Madison Square Garden in New York that ended in the seventh round due to swelling and cuts on Pattersons eye giving the victory to Ali.

On October 1st, 1975, Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier fought for the third time for the World Heavyweight Title. Known as the "Thrilla in Manila," Ali ultimately emerged as the victor in what is considered one of the greatest boxing matches of all time.
On April 1st, 1972 Muhammad Ali and Mac Foster fought in a fifteen round bout that ended in a unanimous decision win for Ali.

programmes.t: Muhammad Ali vs Oscar Natalio Bonavena
programmes.d: On December 7th, 1970 Muhammad Ali faced Oscar Natalio Bonavena in a 15 round bout with Bonavena going down three times in the last round forcing an automatic stoggage giving the win to Ali.

On January 28th, 1974 Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier face eachother for a second time at Madison Square Garden in New York for North American Boxing Federation Heavyweight titles resulting in a strong win for Ali.

On September 10th, 1973 Muhammad Ali and Ken Norton participated in their second meeting at the Forum in Inglewood, CA. They fought for the North American Boxing Federation Heavyweight title with Ali winning this time with split decision.
On October 31st, 2020 Naoya Inoue faced Jason Moloney in The Bubble at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas for the IBF and WBA World Super Bantamweight titles ending in a knockout in the 7th round by Inoue.

programmes.t: Naoya Inoue vs Nonito Donaire II
programmes.d: On June 7th, 2022 Naoya Inoue battled Nonoito Donaire for a second time at the Super Arena in Saitama for IBF, WBA and WBC World Bantamweight title with Inoue ending the bout in the second round defeating Donaire.

On December 15th, 2012 Nonito Donaire faced Jorge Arce at the Toyota Center in Houston, Tx. With the bout ending in the third round with a win by Donaire, Arce announced his retirement in the ring after the bout.

programmes.t: Orlando Salido vs Juan Manuel Lopez 2
programmes.d: On March 10th, 2012, Orlando Salido fought Juan Manuel Lopez for the WBO World Featherweight Title in San Juan, Puerto Rico. In a very entertaining fight with both fighters scoring knockdowns, Salido stopped Lopez in the 10th round.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Curtis Strong
programmes.d: On February 6th, 1993 Oscar De La Hoya and Curtis Strong fought at the Sports Arena in San Diego, Ca. in a 6 round bout that lasted 4 rounds ending in a technical knockout victory for De La Hoya.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Felix Sturm
programmes.d: On June 5th, 2004 Oscar De La Hoya fought Felix Sturm at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas for the WBO Middleweight title in a 12 round bout resulting in an unanimous decision win for De La Hoya.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Fernado Vargas
programmes.d: On September 14th, 2002, Oscar De La Hoya and Fernando Vargas fought for Super Welterweight titles at the Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas. In an incredible battle, De La Hoya was able to stop Vargas in the 11th round.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Giorgio Campanella
programmes.d: On May 27th, 1994 Oscar De La hoya fought Giorgio Campanella at the MGM Grand Garden Arena in Las Vegas for the WBO World Super Featherweight title with De La Hoya knocking out Campanella in the thrid round securing his victory.
Danny checks out an amazing collection, which includes a 1933 Ford Roadster and a '53 Henry J.; Kevin, Ryan and Mike make an unauthorized purchase and the pressure is on Ryan to make it worthwhile.

A returning customer requires Danny's help restoring a 1971 Road Runner to give as a celebratory gift to his wife and step-daughter; Mike and Roli settle a debt by gloving up and taking it to the mat.
Mike buys a Smart car and wants to trick it out at the shop; Danny's pal Shane wants to show Danny his new 1955 Chevy; a special project that will take Danny back to when he first got into cars.

Danny lands a pimp-tastic 1967 Impala, but when it's time to hand the keys over to an important client, Danny doesn't think he can let her go; an old friend shows Danny a 1914 Ford that's headed to the Smithsonian.
Shannon looks to the shop for help with the restoration of a 1962 Karmann Ghia as a present for his wife; Danny gets an invitation of a lifetime.
Kevin is won over by a hot rod pick-up truck; Danny tracks down a customer's original 1969 Firebird; an unannounced visitor causes drama at the shop.
Danny is hosting a giant car show and has to restore a '73 boat-tail Riviera to be the main attraction; Danny finds a collection of jaw-dropping muscle cars.
Danny has plans for a 1972 Cutlass he hopes to flip; Roli looks for help from the guys to learn to do a burn-out; Danny examines a 1971 Torino whose owner can't seem to put a price on it.

Danny has to give up his prized 1972 Monte Carlo for one of his biggest clients, and is counting on his team finish the job done in one week; Ryan and Mike go for the ride of their lives in a 1965 Fastback Mustang.
Danny and the crew build a bike for a woman without a leg; a couple wants a Count's Kustoms bike to do a tour.
Danny has the guys each find and take a picture with their dream car for the Count's Kustoms calendar; Mike and Roli decide to make their own kind of calendar.
The Plymouth Road Runner becomes a nightmare for Kevin when Danny finally buys one; when Kevin tries to shut down the project, Danny pulls a fast one.

Inspired by the Rat Rods at a local shop, Danny sends the guys out to locate parts for a Count's Kustoms Rat Rod; while on the hunt, Danny gets preoccupied by a beauty of a Bel Air and finds himself on the other side of the bargaining table.

programmes.st: October 6, 2015 - Ladies' Night: A Female Empowerment Episode
programmes.d: A baby gets covered in peanut butter, people who try beach proposals struggle to overcome environmental obstacles and a fledgling dancer strips for cash.
Daniel identifies flammable privates and gives away free stuff, and a passionate man with a childish palate gets a Web Redemption.
Daniel turns himself into a human tornado, a brokenhearted teenager gets catfished, and an unexpected threesome participant talks about how it went.

It's week two on the frozen tundra and the name of the game is Rig Move. MGM is breaking down camp and moving every last piece of equipment to a new base at Langley to continue exploring for natural gas.

Day 1 of the new Ice Road season begins. There are 6,000 loads of freight to move in just 12 weeks to the oil camps of Alaska's North Slope. The 400 plus miles stretch from Fairbanks to the remote outpost of Deadhorse.

On Alaska's North Slope, a new ice road season has just begun. Carlile Transportation has less than three months to haul 2,000 loads from Fairbanks to Deadhorse--the gateway to the Prudhoe Bay oil fields.

It's three weeks into the winter season in Northern Alaska, and Carlile Transportation has only moved 500 of the 2,000 loads it needs to transport to the Prudhoe Bay oil fields. The clock is ticking and an arctic storm is brewing.

A massive storm blows in and all traffic on the ice road comes to a standstill. And if wheels aren't turning, no one's earning. George, Tim, and Lisa take shelter at Coldfoot, the only truck stop on the road.

A behavioral profile caused the Baton Rouge Police Department to search for the wrong man. They might not have made an arrest had it not been for a DNA picture of the suspect painted by a molecular biologist.

An obstetrician returned home from the hospital and found his wife on the bathroom floor. She was covered with blood and not breathing. He tried unsuccessfully to revive her, staining his clothes with her blood in the process, and then he called 911.

A Modesto, California, teenager went missing. There was no sign of a struggle in her home, and police suspected she'd simply run away until her naked, bruised body was discovered in a ditch 20 miles away.

When police recovered the submerged car of a man reported missing, they expected to find his body. But it wasn't there. The investigation that followed would uncover an obsession turned deadly and the motive for murder.

Emergency dispatch received a call from a man who said his girlfriend shot and killed herself. The autopsy revealed that the gunshot wound was not self-inflicted, and the evidence on her body would give police a golden opportunity to catch killer.
A Native American woman was brutally killed in the desert of New Mexico, and the crime scene was rich in forensic evidence: tire tracks, shoe impressions, and even the murder weapons.

A brilliant young architect became ill and died just before she was to testify in a criminal trial. The autopsy revealed she'd been poisoned with arsenic. Investigators had to determine which person who knew her had a motive for murder.
An employee of a dry cleaner was raped and murdered in the store. Police turned to forensic science for the answers they needed.

The murder of an eccentric millionaire was not entirely unexpected. He flaunted his wealth and cared little for personal security. The evidence at the crime scene seemed to indicate robbery, but investigators wondered if there was something more.

When a young woman disappeared, police feared she was the latest victim in a string of similar crimes. A pair of bloody gloves, unique tire tracks, and ordinary grass and pine needles provided investigators with some extraordinary clues.

A car carrying three men pulls up alongside another on an Alaskan highway and fires shots, leaving a passenger dead. One of the passengers in the killer's car agrees to testify against his friends. The resulting trials don't end the carnage.
A college student was found dead, and the evidence suggested he knew his killer. Three hairs and some microscopic cells helped police unravel a web of lies and find the motive for murder.

In an affluent suburb of Philadelphia, police were called to the scene of what appeared to be an accidental drowning. The investigation gradually focused on one person, a suspect who had more than a million reasons to want the victim dead.

When two women from the same town were murdered in the same way, police feared a serial killer was on the loose. At first, they thought the victims had nothing in common, until they found tiny clues linking them to the same man.

A teenager went missing after an evening of horseback riding. Her body was found a month later, three miles from her home. The killer unknowingly left trace evidence behind, tiny but unmistakable clues which pointed to him and him alone.

When a popular disc jockey was found murdered in a community garden, police swung into action. A sniffer dog and a blood spatter expert led police to the killer, and he'd been much closer than they realized.

When a man is gunned down in his own garage, police discover that a wound sustained by the grieving widow may have been self-inflicted. They turn to science to help unravel a twisted tale of lust, greed and deception.

Three seemingly unrelated deaths proved to be serial murders. The killer had been careful. He used poison that had no taste or odor. Fortunately for investigators, it also had a unique chemical signature.
When a victim is brutally murdered in his own bed, investigators find a shoe impression in the mud outside: physical evidence they hope will lead to the killer.
Armed with little else, police hoped the shoe impressions found at a Lansing, Michigan, crime scene would put their investigation of Audrey Nichols' murder back on track.

When the head chef of a historic Philadelphia restaurant was found dead, investigators interviewed the usual suspects: family, friends, and co-workers. As they sifted through the evidence, police uncovered a chilling tale of debt and deceit.

When a 30-year-old mother fails to report for duty in Virginia, the Army lists her as AWOL. Her family immediately suspects foul play and embark on a 13-year quest for answers.
In the heart of Cajun country, young mother Brenda DuPont is found murdered in her home in May 1988. The initial investigation sputters and turns cold.
A fire in January 2007 claims the life of WWII vet Bennie Angelo. A closer look at the crime scene reveals Bennie was dead before the fire, bumping an arson case up to homicide.

When the body of 81-year-old Helen Gale is found in her burned-out car, investigators in Southfield, Mich., wonder who would murder this pillar of the community; it will be eight years before a blown alibi brings them face-to face with her killer.

When Chris Green, 19, is found beaten to death in a snowy Bangor, Michigan, ditch in 2002, his family fears their son's murder will never be solved; years pass before shocking revelations from an informant emerge and blow the case wide open.

After it’s flushed down the toilet, a baby alligator grows to monstrous size as it prowls the city sewers. Chaos erupts when it comes to the surface.

Police Lt. Kinderman (George C. Scott) notices similarities between his current murder investigation and the methods used by the Gemini killer (Brad Dourif) who was executed 15 years before. He soon discovers a hospitalized mental patient (Jason Miller) claiming to be the dead serial killer, but who looks uncannily like a priest Kinderman knew who died during an exorcism. As more bodies are found, Kinderman looks for connections between the two supposedly dead men.

Forced by desperate circumstances, two sisters rob a bank and are given instructions to check an old vault, where something dark resides.

Rescued from a shipwreck, a couple soon falls prey to a deranged doctor who wants to use them as incubators for a giant spider's eggs.
A deaf woman is stalked by a killer in her home.

Peter (John Hargreaves) and Marcia (Briony Behets), a bitter married couple teetering on the edge of divorce, take a camping trip to heal the rift between them. As the weekend progresses, the selfish pair engage in reckless behavior that demonstrates an increasing disrespect for their natural surroundings. When Peter and Marcia become the targets of a series of inexplicable animal attacks, it becomes clear that an angry Mother Nature has come to exact her revenge.
A formerly heroic cop returns from the dead and joins forces with a psychotic serial killer to destroy his enemies and settle scores.
Six actresses have been called to an isolated mansion to audition for a movie, but there’s a killer who is determined to kill them all off first.

After a breakdown, a bestselling author retreats to a rural town, only to be tormented by demons and werewolves beyond her imagination.
Decades-old found footage involving three astronauts and an abandoned, secret NASA mission reveals why the U.S. has never returned to the moon.
A psychic and a team of TV ghost hunters travel to New Orleans to investigate a haunted house rumored to be the site of paranormal activity.
An American tourist finds himself becoming involved with a French woman who also happens to be able to supernaturally turn into a werewolf.
Three different horror stories bring a serial killer, a botched hair transplant, and a baseball player to a deranged coroner's morgue.

After an extraordinary season, Monty's orchard has a bountiful harvest of apples and he gives advice on how to pick and store them. Frances Tophill makes a final visit to her shared allotment and joins in with the festivities at their annual show. Adam Frost visits the RHS garden Wisley where he meets the Curator to discuss the effects of summer. Nick Bailey investigates knotweed, one of the most pernicious weeds in the UK, Arit Anderson provides inspiration for colourful late season containers.

As the days get shorter, it is a busy time in the garden. Monty Don cracks on with his seasonal tasks at Longmeadow, giving hints and tips along the way. Carol Klein visits first-time gardeners Dan and Dominique for the very last time.

Adam Frost is at home sharing his love of ornamental grasses, tackling the problem of building a patio on a slope and giving some inspiration on what to plant at the base of a wall. In Margate, the team visit a man who has come up with a unique way of using a shed roof to grow vegetables, and they travel to Swansea to meet inspirational gardener Sue Kent, who shows how she has designed her garden to enable her to garden successfully despite her upper limb difference.

In Leyton, Tariq and Sairah want to turn their dumping ground of a back yard into a sumptuous award-winning garden, suitable for entertaining friends and family. Both have competitive jobs in the banking sector and are used to winning at work but when it comes to gardening, they don't know where to begin.

One couple battle to turn a clay-clogged building site in Sussex into a piece of Portugal. Another tackle a forest of overgrowth in their new back garden in Cadeby. They are determined to create a productive space, something they have always wanted.

A truck driver from Wakefield with a passion for flowers wants to create a perfect outside space for his girlfriend and burgeoning family, while in Swindon a widow wants to find the best way of turning her bleak patch of green into a cottage garden.

Monty Don travels from the north west coast of Scotland to the north east coast of England, from historic reconstructions to modern re-inventions. He visits some of the most inhospitable places in the country and finds gardens that are flourishing.

Monty travels across some of the country's landscapes, heading across the north of England to Northern Ireland. Here, Monty sees the ingenuity, passion and determination of British people to garden and create gardens, no matter what the canvas.
Monty travels across the middle of the country, from Wales to Norfolk. He comes across gardens for gnomes, much-loved, well-tended allotments and extravagant gardens that bankrupted their owners.

Monty Don explores the most densely populated part of the country, London and the home counties. He visits some of London's gardens, including a special one on a barge, as well as a beautifully restored garden close to where he grew up in Hampshire.

Monty travels across the south west of the country to visit some of Britain's most exotic gardens. On this journey, Monty also goes to some of the country's most historic gardens, as well as some challenging contemporary ones.

Monty continues planting up perennials in his recently extended orchard beds and begins a redesign in the dry garden. Toby Buckland explores the impressive collection of heritage daffodils at Cotehele in Cornwall.

It's the Easter bank holiday, and at Longmeadow, Monty turns his attention to planting up his new bog garden, sows cucumber and melon seeds and continues with changes to the dry garden. Adam Frost heads to a beautiful walled garden that is both ornamental and productive in West Sussex. It's the first visit of the year to Sue Kent's garden near Swansea as she reveals news about an exciting new project.
Monty continues his revamp of the dry garden, repots succulents and plants up a window box, while Frances Tophill visits a north London garden which has sustainable produce at its core.

With autumn on the horizon, the seasonal planting of bulbs for spring-flowering begins at Longmeadow. Frances Tophill meets a gardener whose allotment is filled with both traditional and exotic vegetables and Toby Buckland visits The Newt in Somerset to find out about its chequered garden history and to explore its emergence as one of the UK's most exciting gardens.

At Longmeadow this week, Monty reaps a harvest from the vegetable garden, plants up a seasonal pot and gives a masterclass on how to make the perfect compost. Adam Frost travels to York to meet a couple who took on 20 acres of land and filled it with flowers.

Monty gives tips on moving plants which are in the wrong place or have outgrown their space, shows how to store chilies and harvests the last of his tomatoes. Rachel de Thame returns to Longmeadow to talk to Monty about her return to health and to plant up pots for spring colour.

In the last programme of the current series, Monty Don takes stock of his year at Longmeadow. We visit RHS Wisley to learn why autumn leaves are such a precious commodity for our gardens, and in the final instalment of her botany series, Carol Klein celebrates the glorious displays put on by flowering plants to attract pollinators.

Monty Don is at Longmeadow with a host of seasonal jobs to keep his autumn garden looking beautiful for as long as possible, and in the third of her fascinating films about how plants work, Carol Klein investigates the science of stems.

Adam Frost is at home sharing his love of ornamental grasses, tackling the problem of building a patio on a slope and giving some inspiration on what to plant at the base of a wall. In Margate, the team visit a man who has come up with a unique way of using a shed roof to grow vegetables, and they travel to Swansea to meet inspirational gardener Sue Kent, who shows how she has designed her garden to enable her to garden successfully despite her upper limb difference.
Monty gives more advice on tomato-growing, Nick Bailey travels to South Africa in search of the cousins of the Crocosmia, and Advolly Richmond looks at the Victorian trend of garden theme parks.

With Halloween approaching, Monty takes stock of his pumpkins and squashes, plants up alpines and shows how to divide a large fern to create new plants. Meanwhile, Adam Frost and Advolly Richmond visit Hever Castle in Kent.

Adam Frost is in his garden, bringing viewers up to date on how it has been developing, as well as giving advice on growing hydrangeas. Toby Buckland shares his tips on dealing with damaged shrubs, tree pruning and transplanting perennials.

Monty and the team are at RHS Rosemoor in Devon to find out about their fruit trees and sedum collection, and Joe visits Scampston Hall, home of a ten-year experiment in naturalistic planting by garden designer Piet Oudolf.

The team celebrate the bounty our gardens have to offer at this time of year as Carol Klein gathers wild blackberries, Monty Don is at Longmeadow, and we join a champion vegetable grower in Yorkshire as he prepares for the biggest show of the season.

At Longmeadow Monty is planting bulbs in pots and around the garden for an explosion of spring colour. Carol Klein travels to Yorkshire where she takes a close look at the enormous colour range and form of a late season perennial, the salvia. Mark Lane is in Oxfordshire looking at how ornamental grasses can be used in planting design to create exciting combinations.

From giant gooseberries and growing the perfect sweet pea to flamboyant dahlias and plants pollinated by a human hair, this week Monty celebrates the plant passions of some of the extraordinary people featured on the show over the last few years.
Monty's dividing his Pulmonaria and gives advice on frost-protection, Joe visits a tropical oasis outside Bristol, and Carol looks at Rowans from around the world.
Monty's dividing his Pulmonaria and gives advice on frost-protection, Joe visits a tropical oasis outside Bristol, and Carol looks at Rowans from around the world.
Monty Don tackles some seasonal gardening jobs at Longmeadow and guest presenter Matthew Wilson has some ideas to brighten up a dark, north-facing wall.

Monty Don tackles the perennial problem of what to grow in the shade beneath a tree, Carol Klein takes a look at the crocosmia and we meet a gardener in Derbyshire who has spent a lifetime growing and showing gladioli.

It's all about the maintenance this week at Longmeadow, as Monty cuts back and divides spring flowering plants. Joe Swift and Adam Frost meet up in Leicestershire to see how they can help a couple of novice gardeners turn a neglected area of their garden into a useable and useful space. Nick Bailey goes to Ham House in Richmond to see how they are coping with the ravages of box tree caterpillar and Arit Anderson visits a garden in Suffolk to find out about the concept of rewilding.

As autumn gathers momentum, it's time to start putting the garden to bed for winter. Monty Don has some timely advice on what to do. Carol Klein meets a nurseryman in Herefordshire and together they indulge in the beauty of the Japanese maple.

After an extraordinary season, Monty's orchard has a bountiful harvest of apples and he gives advice on how to pick and store them. Frances Tophill makes a final visit to her shared allotment and joins in with the festivities at their annual show. Adam Frost visits the RHS garden Wisley where he meets the Curator to discuss the effects of summer. Nick Bailey investigates knotweed, one of the most pernicious weeds in the UK, Arit Anderson provides inspiration for colourful late season containers.
As the plants in the jewel garden reach the peak of their late summer glory, Monty starts planning for the spring when he plants ferns and gives advice on the care and maintenance of wildlife ponds.

As autumn unfolds in the garden, Monty Don has plenty to be getting on with at Longmeadow. In his quest to track down some of the nations most remarkable allotments, Joe Swift visits a tropical paradise in Runcorn.

It is the autumn equinox and Monty celebrates the season's apple bounty. Monty also plans for Christmas when he plants bulbs to brighten dark winter days, and he gives advice on planting garlic for the following year.

Monty shows how to take cuttings from herbs, prune summer raspberries and plant daylilies. Meanwhile, Adam travels to Whitstable on the Kent coast to see how gardeners cope with the wild, wet and windy weather.

Monty has tips and ideas for planting up garden pots to provide a focal point over the winter months, Rachel visits the tulips of Keukenhof, Joe visits Esther Rantzen's much-loved garden, and Carol visits Glebe Cottage.
Monty is back at Longmeadow, getting stuck into more seasonal tasks. Joe Swift heads to Houghton Lodge Gardens in Hampshire renowned for its walled kitchen garden and heritage fruit collection.

As Monty brings in the summer harvest, he gives advice on what to sow to keep the crops coming up to the end of Autumn. Carol Klein visits a woman who is losing her eyesight and gives her recommendations of plants that will be a feast for her senses.
Not knowing the whole story of Eduardo's (RICK MALAMBRI) accident, will Emma tell Mads and Char about the switch? Sutton comes face to face with Annie Hobbes (STACY EDWARDS).
Emma gets a surprise visit from her creepy foster brother, Travis (KENNETH MILLER), and Sutton is thrown into Emma's old life in Las Vegas.
Emma searches to finally get some answers in the Mercer household, while Sutton tries to pull off her best Emma imitation.
On their 17th birthday, Emma's ideal life is about to come to an end as a vengeful Sutton makes her way back to Phoenix to get her life back.
It's been a tough night for Emma and Ethan, and things get tougher when they find Sutton has disappeared after their argument. Char's aunt (CHARISMA CARPENTER) returns to town.
As an anonymous threat hangs over her head, Emma takes an opportunity to leave town and visit her dad's alma mater. Rebecca (CHARISMA CARPENTER) tries to help Char.
As Emma, Ethan and Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER) seek the truth of what happened to Sutton at the lake, they follow a lead that raises more questions than it answers.
Emma and Ethan's loyalty to each other is strong, but the lies start to take their toll. Laurel and Ted are shocked to discover the motive behind Justin's (RANDY WAYNE) actions.
Trying to help Emma, Ethan heads into a situation that gets out of control. Mads sneaks off to see Ryan (MISHA CROSBY), and Laurel continues to see Justin (RANDY WAYNE).
When Ethan's implicated in a serious crime, he and Sutton hide out with his father, Ben Whitehorse (GIL BIRMINGHAM - The Twilight Saga), on the reservation where he grew up.
Determined to prove Ethan's innocence, Emma takes matters into her own hands, with the help of Mads and Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER).
Arrested on murder charges, Ethan sits in jail as his friends search to prove his innocence. Dan (TYLER CHRISTOPHER) reaches out to an ex-girlfriend who is now a defense attorney.
Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER) starts to doubt Alec's (ADRIAN PASDAR) alibi and begins investigating Rebecca's (CHARISMA CARPENTER) past. Meanwhile, Ethan is avoiding Emma.
In the explosive season finale, Sutton encourages Emma to show Kristin what they found in Rebecca's (CHARISMA CARPENTER) house, and Ethan makes a discovery that changes the game.
In the season premiere, Alec (ADRIAN PASDAR) is in jail after his arrest for murder, but he still manages to unnerve Emma. Rebecca and Sutton formulate plans for the Mercer family.
Sutton steps up her plans to win back Ethan. Feeling left out of Emma and Thayer's (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER) growing closeness, Mads shocks Emma with a family revelation.
Sutton decides she wants her life back in order to spend more time with Ethan, and Laurel asks Jordan (recurring guest star RYAN ROTTMAN) out on a very awkward date.
Rebecca uses Sutton to further her agenda, and Emma learns that Sutton may not have told her the whole story about the night her car went in the lake.
Laurel begins asking questions about Sutton's radical personality changes and Emma renews her search for her birth mother.
The school formal creates new opportunities for secrets and lies to be revealed when everyone ends up with the wrong partner. Emma turns to Ethan for help.
Emma struggles to make sense of newfound revelations and shifts in her relationships with Ethan and Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER). Sutton and Rebecca's bond may start to crack.
Everyone gathers to celebrate the wedding of Dan (TYLER CHRISTOPHER) and Theresa (YARA MARTINEZ), but the celebration does not go off as planned. Ethan confronts Emma.

In the dramatic season one finale, Christopher and Elena begin to learn that not everyone is as they appear to be. Long-buried secrets are revealed as the past rears its ugly head.
In the second season premiere, as Christopher seeks to gain the upper hand in his divorce from Rebecca Sutter, a game-changing revelation turns everything on its head.
Pamela Rebecca Barnes schemes with John Ross to fulfill her father's desire for revenge. Ryland's mother (JUDITH LIGHT) proves just as evil as her son.
Pamela pushes her father's agenda to gain control of Ewing Energies. As a new member of the family arrives at Southfork, Ann is pushed to the brink by Ryland's sadistic games.
J.R. works to undermine Pamela, forcing John Ross to choose between a Ewing and a Barnes. Cliff Barnes (KEN KERCHEVAL) returns to meet with an unlikely visitor.
John Ross' plot to take over Ewing Energies solidifies; Christopher changes tactics with Pamela Barnes; and an enemy from the Ewings' past resurfaces.

In the aftermath of John Ross and Sue Ellen's coup, Bobby's brother Gary (TED SHACKELFORD) helps him retaliate. Christopher and John Ross clash in a winner-takes-all car race.
J.R. Ewing finally meets his end. The family strives to set aside their differences and mourn together. Accompanied by many characters from J.R.'s past, the Ewings bury their own.
Bobby, Christopher and John Ross work on J.R.'s masterpiece. J.R.'s will has lasting effects on the family legacy. Sue Ellen tries to get Gary (TED SHACKELFORD) out of Dallas.
Pamela's mother, Afton Cooper (AUDREY LANDERS), returns to Dallas. Emma is put in the middle of her father and grandmother's relationship, pushing her closer to Drew.
The Ewings' investigation of a conspiracy continuing to blame Christopher for recent events brings revelations in line with J.R.'s masterpiece. A new adversary is added to the mix.
After Cliff (KEN KERCHEVAL) and Ryland put Ewing Energies on the verge of collapse, the Ewings battle back. Christopher gets closer to finding his mother.

After a series of brutal bank robberies and murders in south Miami during the mid-1980's, the FBI embarked on an exhaustive eight-month investigation.  With little evidence and no suspects, agents were willing to try anything to find the violent perpetrators.  On April 11, 1986, agents conducting routine surveillance spotted the vehicle used in the bank robberies.  They attempted to arrest the two suspects in the car.  What followed was the bloodiest firefight in FBI history.

Beginning in summer of 1990, the bodies of several women began turning up in and around the city of Vienna, Austria. From an extensive investigation by the Viennese police, it was determined that these murders were the work of one sadistic predator.  Europe was dealing with a serial killer.  With no experience with this kind of predator, Viennese police turned to the FBI. FBI profilers were able to identify a suspect in the murders. On August 20, 1980, an unseen sniper murdered two young black men as they jogged with two white women in Salt Lake City, Utah.  Police threw all their resources into finding a killer who left almost no clues behind.  They met with FBI agents and detectives from around the country who had similar racially motivated sniper slayings.  A month later, working off little more than a possible license plate number, police in Kentucky arrested Joseph Paul Franklin but the man escaped from custody.

By April of 1995 in Washington, D.C., two officers had been shot and one had been murdered. Each had been sitting in their patrol cars when a man sneaked up and opened fire. The FBI was brought in to help catch the cop killer.  Agents identified the man who was most likely the killer, but he was nowhere to be found.  Months of surveillance operations around the country finally yielded a break; they found their suspect in Baltimore, MD.

Racial tensions in Buffalo in 1980 were at an all-time high.  Six black males had been brutally murdered--two had their hearts cut out.  The only thing connecting the victims was their ethnicity and the fact that each had been shot with .22 caliber bullets. Residents screamed for the police to stop this serial killer.  With no suspects, local investigators turned to the FBI.  Profilers were able to produce a psychological composite of the type of person the killer would most likely be.  Their an

On February 3, 1990, a 14-year-old girl ran away from her mother's home and disappeared without a trace.  Her mother hoped Pasadena, Texas police could find her before it was too late.  Six months later, their worst fear was realized when a farmer discovered the young girl's remains in an Illinois barn.  The FBI was called in to help.  Agents tracked down a trucker who they believed was responsible for 50 more deaths.  Investigators knew they had to stop this menace of the highways.

When a Delaware woman vanished in 1996, family and friends discovered her secret life.  The appointments secretary to the Governor had carried on an illicit affair with a wealthy married man.  Agents suspected that her powerful ex-lover was responsible, but they had little physical evidence to support their theory.  Investigators never found the woman's body or the murder weapon.  The FBI's only hope was to go undercover, and turn brother against brother.

In the early 90s, Washington, D.C. police were losing the battle against street gangs who enforced their territories with lethal violence.  The homicide rate in the nation's capital climbed to the highest in the country.  Local police turned to the FBI for help, but agents soon found themselves in the direct line of fire.  In the fall of 1994, a gang member walked into police headquarters, killed two FBI agents and one detective, then turned the gun on himself.

In June of 1992, masked bandits pulled off a daring mid-day bank robbery.  It marked the beginning of a four-year crime wave that rocked Seattle.  With each new robbery, the bandits perfected their craft, leaving behind no evidence and escaping with hundreds and thousands of dollars.  As the robbers became increasingly violent, pressure mounted to end their reign.  With few leads, the FBI forced their own luck.  The effort put them face to face with an armed and desperate fugitive.

When police in a small Washington State community began looking into the disappearance of a 22-year-old woman, they had no way of knowing it would evolve into a nationwide hunt for a sexual sadist.  Police knew the killer's identity, but he was a master of disguise.  The FBI was called on to help.  Agents discovered that several unsuspecting women across the northwest had fallen prey to his charms.

A stranger snatched an eight-year-old girl as she played in her Tucson, Arizona neighborhood, leaving behind an abandoned bicycle and a frantic mother.  Hundreds of citizens and police officers fanned out across the region, hoping to find some trace of the young girl or her abductor.  Within hours, a suspect emerged; a drifter who was out on parole for abducting and molesting children.  He was nowhere to be found and time had run out for the innocent child.

On a chilly afternoon in 1989, Marine Captain Shirley Russell disappeared from Quantico, Virginia.  Captain Russell was a dedicated officer; her friends and colleagues were certain she had not gone AWOL.  FBI agents found her husband, a former Marine, was acting strangely, and a blood-like stain on the couple's floor disappeared before agents could examine it.  There was no body, no witness and no weapon.

In February of 1996, New Jersey millionaire Frank Black flew to Florida to close a major business deal before retiring.  He never came home.  Authorities in New Jersey sensed foul play and brought in the FBI.  Agents learned of a mystery woman in Florida who was to meet Black.  Phone records showed a flood of calls to Black from his business rival just before the disappearance.

In 1997, FBI agents began investigating New York gas station mogul Gurmeet Dhinsa for gas pump rigging.  They soon realized that Dhinsa was more than a crooked businessman, he enforced his mob-like operation with brutal violence, kidnapping and killing errant employees and any family members who questioned their deaths.  FBI agents worked their way into Dhinsa's violent world.

In the early 1980s, the decapitation of a young African-American male led the Miami-Dade police department and the FBI along a trail of murder.  Investigators quickly discovered that the victim was a dissident member of a religious sect headed by a man calling himself Yahweh ben Yahweh, or God, Son of God.  Although the FBI believed Yahweh ben Yahweh and his followers were responsible for many murders, they could find no direct evidence linking them to the crimes.

In November of 1994, when a Wells Fargo armored van disappeared from a Glendale, Arizona mall, local authorities and the FBI scrambled to recover it, and its cargo of nearly a million dollars. Six hours later, agents found the van, its driver shot dead inside and the money gone. It was a perfect hit by professionals who left no clue behind. Months passed before a solid lead developed. In January, a tip led agents to look into a former prison guard.

Beginning in California in 1995, a serial killer targeted vulnerable women. At first charming and generous, he quickly became violent. He was brutal with his kills and quick in his getaways. Traveling across the country, he struck in Mississippi, Louisiana and Florida. The FBI and local police needed to stop this cross-country killer before more women fell victim to his insatiable rage.

In 1987, a successful television producer was gunned down in his New York office.  It looked like a professional hit.  With no leads, the investigation stalled.  Four years later and a continent away, a man told Los Angeles police he had been hired to murder two exotic dancers.  Investigators linked the two crimes and uncovered a businessman willing to kill to protect his interests.

A 1981 armored car robbery near New York City left one guard dead and another critically wounded.  Police stopped suspects nearby and another shoot-out ensued, claiming the lives of two officers.  Local police and the FBI suspected a large group of domestic terrorists with a history of violent crime.  They would try to ferret out these heavily armed criminals who moved in a shadowy underworld and were not afraid to kill authorities.

When a California man was found dismembered in 1990, police suspected a local burglar, but they couldn't find him.  Six months later, he was caught robbing an Arizona bank and sentenced to life.  But prison couldn't hold him for long, and within a year he escaped.  The FBI would lead a multi-agency manhunt for a killer on a desperate run through the tourist regions of the west.

At first it seemed like a tragic hunting accident when 18-year-old David Wilkey was shot to death in rural Virginia in 1983.  A tenacious insurance investigator suspected foul play, but he had no direct evidence. Two years later a man contacted North Carolina FBI agents with a complex story of conspiracy and murder-for-hire: he claimed he had been hired to murder Wilkey's killer.

On a summer night in 1990, a body was discovered burning in a Minnesota alley.  Weeks later, police finally identified the victim, a suspected drug courier from California.  The FBI began working with local police and slowly uncovered a multi-state crime ring run by a deadly drug lord who used violence and intimidation to keep those around him silent.  Agents needed to infiltrate and dismantle the crew before more people died.

In the early 1990's drug gangs terrorized Harlem, New York neighborhoods. When a 10-year-old boy fell victim in the crossfire, NYPD detectives and FBI agents clamped down on the problem. They formed a task force called C-11, designed to dismantle the gangs. In an environment of violence and fear it would be difficult to identify, arrest and convict those involved in the secretive and deadly world of big money drugs.

In 1994, a teenage immigrant came to the United States to realize her dream of becoming a doctor.  But a tragic twist of fate intervened, when she found herself an innocent victim of the drug trade.  Kidnapped and held captive, she survived for days against all odds.  Authorities arrested her captors, but they refused to reveal her whereabouts. The FBI and local police raced against time, determined to save the teenager's life. Their investigation revealed a complex story of drugs, betrayal and

In the mid-1990's, a gang of professional bank robbers raided cities across seven states. Disguises and speed protected their identity from cameras and the police as they stole hundreds of thousands of dollars, always leaving a bomb to terrorize their victims. The stakes were raised when the FBI discovered the robbers had an agenda beyond their personal wealth. To stop these extremists and their growing operation, the FBI needed to capture their leaders.

A Labor Day weekend turned into a nightmare of murder as a cross-country crime spree terrorized the nation.  In a small Ohio community, an elderly woman and a teenage boy disappeared within hours of each other.  Police believed the cases were linked, but didn't know how. They contacted the FBI for help.  A trail of stolen vehicles and murder victims across seven states led agents on a hunt for two suspected killers. Their only hope of stopping them was to anticipate the killers' next move.

A day that began with a class field trip ended with a parent's worst nightmare.  An 11-year-old girl was missing.  Her parents were certain she was no runaway.  When they failed to find her in their quiet Illinois neighborhood, they called the police.  The FBI soon joined the investigation and family and friends worked with detectives and agents in an urgent search for the missing girl.  Faced with conflicting witness reports and false leads, agents wouldn't stop until they found the girl, and t

In the summer of 1988, a wealthy Jackson, Mississippi woman disappeared from her home in broad daylight.  Left behind was a mysterious ransom note listing twelve names and no specific instructions.  The note, and a few drops of blood were the only clues to her fate. FBI and local police struggled to find answers in the cryptic message so they could find the kidnapper and retrieve the victim before her time ran out. Solving the crime required the keen insight of a criminal profiler and the persev

In Arizona, a shipment of money vanished into the high desert, along with the two men hired to guard it.  The FBI didn't know if the guards were participants or victims of an ambush.  Answers lay somewhere in the thousands of square miles of Arizona's northwest territory.  When the vehicle was recovered with three hundred thousand dollars and the drivers missing, suspicions that the crime was an inside job grew.

In Alabama, a pair of convicted felons escaped the custody of a local deputy and fled across the country.  Eluding authorities, they moved from state to state in a wave of abduction and car theft.  When a foreign military officer disappeared along their trail, police and FBI agents wondered if the armed fugitives had become killers.  Agents believed the pair were growing more violent and raced to find the escapees before more victims crossed their path.

In 1992, a young mother was gunned down in front of her children.  Police searched for answers, but found none. The horrible crime appeared unmotivated, senseless, and random. Then, family members offered a startling clue.  The victim, the wife of a prominent Atlanta attorney, was also a woman burdened with a secret; a secret the FBI believed led to her death.  It would force local and federal agents to untangle an intricate web of money, drugs and murder.

In Memphis, Tennessee, a horrible crime terrified local residents.  When a wealthy young mother was abducted in front of her in-laws' home, the police had no shortage of suspects.  The twenty-five year old victim left behind a tumultuous marriage, an ex-husband, and several spurned boyfriends.  All were on the FBI's short list.  To find the woman and her abductor, investigators would have to first determine the motive.

In 1997, a series of crimes in a small Iowa farming community left residents reeling in shock and fear. Two young men went on a crime spree of robbery, kidnapping and murder, and then disappeared. By the time they were identified, they already had a twelve-hour lead. As the hunt for the two men expanded, the FBI committed its resources to tracking down the suspects. The pursuit would take agents across six states to catch the killers before they struck again.

In the late 80's, Florida's cocaine imports were among the highest in the nation.  Regional territories were enforced with intimidation and murder.  Desperate to stop the violence, local authorities turned to the FBI for help. One dealer bowed to no one.  He would stop at nothing to keep detectives and agents from building a case against him.  When his organization began targeting the government itself, a city went on high alert.

In Kokomo, Indiana an unthinkable crime terrified residents. A young woman was snatched from her home on a bright spring morning.  Drops of blood and a torn window screen were all that was left to tell authorities what happened to the twenty-one year old victim. After several days of searching, a former FBI profiler narrowed the suspect list to one. Agents and detectives followed the trail across state lines hoping to find the victim before her time ran out.

In July 1997, a triple murder terrified residents in the nation's capital. In a Georgetown coffee shop, three employees were shot to death. Investigators could find no immediate suspects and no clear motive for the attack. Evidence at the crime scene pointed in many different directions. Was this a hate crime, a robbery gone wrong, or an act of cold-blooded vengeance against one of the victims?

In 1986, a small crime free Indiana town was turned inside out by the arrival of one dangerous stranger. After an officer was gunned down at point-blank range, the psychotic killer led investigators across the Midwest. No one knew where the gunman would strike next, even as his tally of murders and abductions grew. The FBI and state police raced against time to rescue America's heartland from this deranged gunman, before he killed again.

In Langley, Virginia, a gunman fired into rush hour traffic.  The brazen daytime shooting of employees from the Central Intelligence Agency stunned the country.  The victims seemed randomly selected, but the motive appeared to be political. The FBI was called in, but the nationwide search quickly became a far-reaching international manhunt. Agents processed more than 2000 leads and crossed an ocean in the effort to deliver justice.

On the day before Thanksgiving, a mother discovered her 10 year-old son was missing from his school. No one knew how it could have happened.  Within hours, the boy's entire family was frantically searching for him. The few leads in the case quickly turned cold and the FBI was called in to aid in the investigation. The search by agents and local authorities would cover a thousand miles to expose the kidnapper and find the missing child.

On a summer afternoon in upscale Lodi, California, a 12-year-old girl is abducted from her home.  Scores of police officers and FBI agents converge, determined to find the young girl before it is too late.  When the kidnapper's car is discovered in a field near Lodi, police dogs, helicopters, and hundreds of volunteers are employed in a round-the-clock search.  It would take a community united in concern for one of their youngest to find the missing child.

In rural Texas, 13-year-old is kidnapped on her way to school.  Frantic to find her safely, her millionaire father calls local authorities and the FBI.  As police officers and agents conduct aerial surveillance, the father drives hundreds of miles through the night to deliver the ransom cash to a drop that the kidnappers keep changing.  In a final effort to save the young girl, investigators must engage in a dangerous firefight with five desperate criminals.

In September 1997, a team of masked gunmen robbed an armored car facility in Los Angeles, and made off with $18.9 million, the largest takeover heist in U.S. history.  An employee believed she recognized the voice of one of the robbers, and FBI agents began conducting surveillance on a former employee of the facility.  With only one piece of physical evidence, a fragment of a vehicle taillight, authorities hoped to connect him to the crime, and locate his accomplices.

programmes.d: In the heart of the Balearic Islands, AE Illes Balears Palma has redefined futsal. More than a team, it’s a culture built on ambition and unity. From humble beginnings to UEFA Futsal Champions League dominance, AE Illes Balears Palma’s story is one of resilience and excellence. This film dives into the soul of the club—its traditions, victories, and the people who made it a symbol of futsal supremacy.

programmes.t: VIVA PALMA - An Illes Balears Palma Futsal Story
programmes.d: In the heart of the Balearic Islands, AE Illes Balears Palma has redefined futsal. More than a team, it’s a culture built on ambition and unity. From humble beginnings to UEFA Futsal Champions League dominance, AE Illes Balears Palma’s story is one of resilience and excellence. This film dives into the soul of the club—its traditions, victories, and the people who made it a symbol of futsal supremacy.

What ever happened to the “Old Chevy,” you ask? That is one of the most common questions we get at Chronicle. Longtime Chronicle co-anchor Peter Mehegan and his trusty ’69 Chevy logged a lot of miles together in Maine. For those of you who missed those years, and those who miss the Chevy (and Peter), tonight is a look back.

Here’s a suggestion for beating the dog days of summer – stay inside watching a show about actual dogs! We visit outdoor dining destinations in Boston and Salem where you can bring your four-legged friend (including one that serves dogs their meals on a take-home frisbee).

Service dogs, K-9 officers – even a four-legged doggie influencer with his own glam squad and “momager.” Tonight we meet some of these working dogs – as well as other animals with day jobs. At NEADS World Class Service Dogs we meet puppies prepping for a career of service. The “employees” of Goats to Go help businesses tame out-of-control vegetation, while the mini-horses of Lifting Spirits connect with people in need of comfort and support. It’s our birthday! Chronicle debuted on Jan. 25, 1982, and we’re inviting you to help us celebrate with a week of classic Chronicle shows – all leading up to a jam-packed, prime-time special! Tonight we flash back to 1987 when it was “Big Apple or Bust” for the Chronicle crew. Mary Richardson took to the skies, Peter Mehegan hit the highway, and Mike Barnicle boarded the train. Who hit New York City’s Plaza Hotel first? Come along for the ride and find out!

Tonight we go backstage at local theaters, each with its own rich history – each celebrating a major milestone. Also tonight, a sit-down with jazz legend Herbie Hancock ahead of his recent performance at the Boch Center Wang Theater.

Erika Tarantal loves children, so it is no surprise some of her favorite stories this year were stories about children: keeping kids engaged with learning, giving them access to healthy activities, and connecting children to the environment. Tonight, a rundown of Erika’s 2021 highlights from her “Five for Good” series.
It’s that time of year, when we look back at the stories we’ve shared with you throughout the year – and the generous people who have shared their stories with us. Erika Tarantal's favorites.

Nicole Estaphan brings us eye-catching, eye-popping, “eye candy!” She meets artist Howie Green, famed for his colorful “pop-up” pop art, and discovers shoes that will blow your mind (and benefit good causes). In Winsted, Conn. Nicole checks out a 5-story-high mural that took 22 years to complete. You can’t eat these Tootsie Rolls or Necco wafers – they’re works of art by a bead artist whose work is featured at a local gallery. Tonight Erika Tarantal brings us beautiful things and the people who create them.

Tonight we test whether New Englanders can agree on what qualifies as acceptable etiquette, from “manspreading” on the T to lane-cutting on Storrow Drive. Tune in to find out which very opinionated New Englander we invite to weigh in as our celebrity judge.

Just a quick hop from Boston, but it feels a million miles away. Tonight Shayna Seymour explores the pink sand beaches and bluer-than-blue waters of Bermuda, a beloved destination for Boston-area travelers.

We go “behind closed doors” of the Boston Public Library to view a handwritten letter from Frederick Douglass and books that belonged to John Adams. Grief or tragedy can be difficult to explain. Some believe art can be a healthy way to express feelings that can’t be put into words. Tonight, Nicole Estaphan shares stories of people finding their voices through art including a young woman using dance to deal with her father’s past imprisonment; an artist teaching others to paint through the pain of grief;  and music as therapy.

Think you face challenges on the golf course? Tonight Nicole Estaphan meets a top-ranked young golfer, an amputee, who is working to advance the sport of adaptive golf and inspiring others along the way. Nicole brings us the story of a young family committed to supporting others while managing their own toddler’s severe illness – and his father’s battle with cancer. The holiday season can compound feelings of grief or loneliness. Tonight we talk with those who have experienced those emotions and developed ways to power through.

Iconic, aluminum travel trailers sound like a throwback, and they are. But at an Airstream “campground” on Cape Cod, Erika Tarantal discovers this retro vehicle has undergone some modern upgrades. Nicole Estaphan spends the night in a refurbished 100-year-old train caboose in Chester, Mass. And once you crash at one vehicle-turned-hotel, why not try another? Nicole spends the night on a 43-foot motor yacht moored in Charlestown. Join us as we check-in to some “Rare” BnBs.

Erika explores the next-generation market Portugalia, which highlights high-end goods from Portugal. A picture is worth a thousand words, and thanks to technology we all have the ability to capture powerful images. We visit the Griffin Museum of Photography in Winchester to discuss how that’s changing the landscape.

Tonight, we are exploring the world of folk art, from the storied collection at Boston’s Museum of Fine Arts to collectibles crafted by hand in a Sutton studio. We find a treasure trove of historic weathervanes and consult the experts at Skinner on what’s hot. And are tattoos folk art? We’ll have the answer.

From family businesses to legacy brands and products - we are getting the stories behind them all.

Boston culinary icon Lydia Shire is still cooking, still creating – and still inspiring! Tonight she takes us from Chinatown to Cambridge, exploring the dishes and traditions that fuel her imagination—from roast duck to homemade lemongrass oil.

To prove how trendy he is, Ben accompanies an embarrassed Michael to a gay club, where he gets chatted up by the adoring Rupert, who follows him home and sends him flowers.
Whilst Susan is away Ben takes part in a police identity parade, where he is picked out as being a mugger and remanded in a cell with hard cases Carl and Terry.
When Janey has to sit with a poorly Kenzo, Ben volunteers to look after one of her elderly care clients, Harry, a man who seems to have been around but is not allowed out.
Ben and Susan have yet another row after he refuses to attend her godparents' anniversary party so they decide on a trial separation, taking it in turns to live in the house alone.

Bannister fills in for Murray's dad on a father and son wilderness survival test.

Marlene introduces Christian to her friend Barbara and the two of them have an instant attraction to each other. He is shocked to learn that Barbara has a 10 year old son. Bannister is planning on hosting a circus.
Alf puts makeup on an attractive lady shopping which leads to them going on a date. The freezers in the store blows up, and there's a mad scramble to keep the food frozen.
While showing his children's birthday party routine to Edna, TC arrives at Cobb's with a corporate psychiatrist.

The staff pose for the camera in bowling uniforms. They're trying to win a local bowling competition with a grand prize of 3,000. Edna wants to bowl, but Howard will only let her if someone else gets hurt. When their lead bowler breaks his arm, the store scrambles to find a replacement,
When Leslie announces that he will be attending a seminar for potential investors, he asks Bannister to go with him. Bannister, willing to do anything to miss the Opera with Edna, reluctantly agrees.

Helen hires Stanley's friend, Joey, to haul out their furniture so she can redecorate. Her brother in law, Hubert, hears of Helen's plan and decides to buy some new furniture. Joey offers to sell his furniture for him and sells it to Stanley. When Helen sees he bought her sister's furniture she freaks out.

Helen really wants an electric organ but Stanley won't pay for one. Anne has an emergency and asks Helen to do her a favor by showing a buyer some property. An embarrassing situation may complicate things.

Jeffrey Brookes has a secret. His Uncle Bill is a free spirited "hobo" who has no interest in material things. To his horror, Bill shows up at his doorstep...but not before Stanley meets him and hires Bill to help around his place.

Running out of money, Stanley needs to take a job on the killing floor at his brother-in-law Hubert's meat packing plant. Later, his fortunes change when he learns Hubert is planning a secret trip to Acapulco with his secretary.

When Stanley is being inattentive towards Helen, she decides to make him jealous by pretending to have an affair with the gardener. Both Anne and Jeffrey Brookes decide to help out and also hire some other guys to pose as Helen's lover.
A young woman without a place to live has been sleeping in the Ropers' storage room. Stanley thinks the girl is a dangerous "dope fiend" while Helen wants to let her stay.
Ethel tries to get a china horse, supposedly from the Ming Dynasty, away from Helen.
Mr. Roper decides to fix Jenny up with Brookes' nephew and Brookes freaks out upon learning about it.
Helen's and David's birthday party is a disaster when first Stanley and Jeffrey and then Helen and Anne start squabbling.
Helen is convinced Stanley is having an affair when she sees him give a locket to another women.
Helen volunteers Stanley to babysit on his poker night.

Jack and Vicky argue over money. Mr. Bradford offers to pay for sprinklers that Jack needs for the bistro if Jack can convince Vicky to marry him.
To get Vicky to accept his standing marriage proposal, Jack attempts to reunite Vicky's divorced parents. First appearance of Mrs. Bradford.
James moves in to care for Vicky when she comes down with the measles.
Jack seeks advice from a psychologist about his recent impotence. Vicky thinks Jack is cheating on her with E.Z.'s girlfriend Susie.
Vicky and Jack try to spend time sharing each others' non-sexual interests.

Jack mistakenly believes that Vicky's friend is coming onto him.
Jack convinces Vicky to invest in a case of vintage wine, but when it turns out to be sour, he takes a job at a sushi house to repay her.
Jack grooms E.Z. for a date with a high-class girl who only seems interested in Jack.
With his ego bruised after to losing a trivia game to Vicky, Jack tries to best her but ends up embarrassing himself at a beach carnival in front of guests.
After Jack and James get drunk together, James is arrested for urinating in public and ends up in court.
Jack's old friend, Larry invites him to a swinging party where an old flame makes a move on Jack.
After Jack saves James' life, James finds Jack to be the son he never had.
With his restaurant suddenly popular after a glowing review, Jack forgets about his and Vicky's first anniversary.
Jack butts heads with James on a radio debate show.
When Jack and Vicky are cast in a commercial for her airline, Jack fights with the temperamental director.
Stanley fears Helen accidentally gave a box containing his girlie magazines to a church rummage sale.

Stanley is jealous when Helen wants to reunite with an old boyfriend who is in town, so he tries to reconnect with an old girlfriend to get even with her. Also, David trades Jeffrey's model train set for Stanley's old inner tube.

Helen and her sisters are shocked by their elderly mother wanting to have a 'wake' for herself. She invites others to say goodbye in advance. Also, Jeffrey throws his back out and is trapped in a chair.
The Brookes are expecting a Congressman to drop by and Jeffrey doesn't want the Ropers around when he comes.
Stanley's physical checkup for a life insurance policy has him convinced his days are numbered.
Mrs. Roper thinks her husband is having an affair when she finds his hidden stash of love letters , written to a woman named Doris.

Helen's mother comes for a visit. But later it is revealed that she has no place to go. So Helen and her two sisters get together to decide what to do, cause none of them really want her living with them.

Helen's luncheon makes her consider leaving the Cheviot Hills neighborhood. Stanley believes her and, without asking, has Jeffrey Brookes put their home on the market. Will The Ropers really relocate?

A man shows up and claims to be Stanley's son. Stanley admits to know his mother, but doesn't remember the night that she claimed to conceive her son. Roper goes to talk to a friend who was with him at the time to find out if the claims are true.
Helen adores the Brookes' boy, David, which leads her to feel she and Stanley could adopt a baby. Stanley is against it. Still, she calls an agency and sets up a home interview.

Frost's investigation into a woman's death exposes the secret life of respectable rural England.

Marga's way of coping with finding out the truth about Daniela lands her in hot water. In the aftermath of her actions, she finally comes to terms with her feelings for her mother.

Isabel overhears Carlos's incriminating call with Rigor. Fearing she'll expose him, Carlos moves to silence her. As the Agbayanis mourn Maila, Roman learns of Bianca's suspicions.

When Chelsea Simms, the good-hearted brand strategist for the popular dating app The Nice List, discovers the app has granted her magical powers, she uses her newfound ability to make all of the �naughty� people in her life learn how to be good again. But when her plans go awry and Fisher, the kindly neighbor who has always carried a torch for Chelsea, is magically added to the naughty list by mistake, Chelsea must race against time to set things right before Christmas Eve.

In a small Texas town during the holiday season, Ethan, a meteorologist, is woken in the middle of the night for a call about a tornado that has just hit. His wife Addison, a TV news reporter, is also summoned to work to do a piece on the tornado for the morning news.  Ethan realizes the conditions are ripe for more tornadoes.

A quiet, ordinary man sees his comfortable life turned upside down at Christmas when he discovers his wife is having an affair and wants a divorce. Suddenly facing the holidays alone, he struggles to find any reason to celebrate. But an unexpected friendship with a kindhearted volunteer Santa helps him rediscover hope, joy and the magic of the season, leading him on a heartfelt journey toward healing, new possibilities and a Christmas miracle he never saw coming.

Haley Foster built a big city life in Los Angeles as a top wedding planner at an elite and powerful company run by Ms. Reynolds. When her sister, Angela, insists on getting married Christmas Day on the tree farm in their old hometown of Truxton, Haley is resigned to make her sister’s dreams come true and her parents happy.

Jessica has a big presentation in Palm Springs. There are a couple of problems though: her two kids who will do anything to get mom and dad back together again - even if they have to hack mom's phone or pose as a secretary to make sure dad's in Palm Springs too. And father Joe who'll do anything to charm his way back into Jessica's life.

This Christmas, Riley Harper fights to save her small-town animal rescue from closing. Across the ocean, Prince Edward of Arendale travels to America to secure a land deal—unaware the property belongs to Riley. When fate (and a lost dog tag) brings them together, sparks fly. But when Riley learns Edward’s true identity, her trust shatters. On Christmas Eve, Edward risks it all to save her shelter—and her heart.

When brilliant and sharp-witted archaeologist Lucy Stewart decides to spend her Christmas break in the Scottish Highlands, she goes on a quest to find the ruins of a shrine to an ancient goddess.  Through her journey, she learns the importance of letting a little festive wonder back into her life and discovers both history and love along the way.

When brilliant and sharp-witted archaeologist Lucy Stewart decides to spend her Christmas break in the Scottish Highlands, she goes on a quest to find the ruins of a shrine to an ancient goddess.  Through her journey, she learns the importance of letting a little festive wonder back into her life and discovers both history and love along the way.

Heather, a hardworking mall manager, must make tough holiday cuts—including ending leases on struggling stores—to earn a promotion. Focused on her career, she’s given up on love, but her spirited niece Molly hasn’t. Molly asks the mall Santa for a Christmas boyfriend for Heather—unaware he’s actually Ryan, a mall worker secretly helping his aunt’s failing toy shop. Can love survive their hidden truths?

Emily is determined to fulfil her father�s wishes to save the family dairy farm which has been financially struggling for years.  When a handsome stranger, Charlie, shows up at Emily�s family dairy farm at Christmastime, Emily has to hide her feelings for him when he turns out to be her sister�s partner and they are there to sell the farm. Can Emily get her Christmas miracle to save the family farm and win the handsome guy in the end?

Emily is faced with the daunting task of fulfilling her late mother Ruby’s last wish – a twelve-task Christmas Checklist. With local freelance writer Noah covering her compelling story, his article turns from inspiring to cherished just in time for Christmas Eve, as their journey together reveals that Ruby’s final wish has been in front of them the whole time.

Single father, Tom and his daughter, Grace make the big move from the sunny land of Australia to the quaint US town of Ashbury Grove. While exploring her new backyard, Grace finds a mysterious time capsule, containing a guide to a perfect family Christmas. The two tasks themselves with finding its owner which leads them to finding love and their own perfect family Christmas.

Daisy, a determined real estate broker, inherits her grandfather’s ranch just before Christmas. Focused on selling, she returns home only to reconnect with Ben, her childhood crush who now works as a ranch hand. As holiday traditions stir memories and rekindle old feelings, Daisy begins to question the fast-paced career she’s built. With the season drawing to a close, she must decide between ambition and love.

A big-city relationship expert, famous for dishing out advice on her hit talk show, finds her carefully curated life unraveling when she gets stranded at a small-town ranch just before Christmas. Forced to trade cameras and cue cards for chores and quiet nights, she clashes—and sparks—with the rugged rancher who takes her in. As holiday magic weaves around them, she learns that love, unpolished and unscripted, could be her most life-changing lesson.

An ambitious hotel manager returns to her hometown for Christmas, planning only a short visit at her family’s charming B&B. To her surprise, the inn is booked solid—with her three high school exes among the guests. As old rivalries resurface and sparks fly, she’s swept into a holiday whirlwind of laughter, mishaps, and second chances. Amid the festive chaos, she discovers love may have been waiting all along.

Morgan has lost her Christmas spirit after breaking up with her long time boyfriend, Liam. She decides to go to a retreat called The Christmas Lonely Hearts Club where she hopes to rekindle her Christmas spirit. Things seem to be going well until her Ex shows up. Morgan and Liam will have to conceal their previous relationship while trying to discover what it means to be single. What they don’t realize is that adhering to the “no romance” policy might require a Christmas miracle.

An ad executive, overwhelmed by work, is granted a magical do-over of the holidays by Santa. As she relives the same festive days, she begins to recognize how much time she’s missed with her family. Through the repeating moments, she learns to slow down, cherish loved ones, and find balance between career and personal life. The story highlights the importance of connection, presence, and appreciating the people who matter most.

A single, successful writer decides to do double duty when her best friend invites her on a Christmas Cruise and decides to see if finding true love during the holidays can really happen or will it be just another holiday story.

When Ashley Seever returns home for the holidays hoping to reconnect with her high school sweetheart Grant, she soon meets his new girlfriend. In an attempt to escape the embarrassment, she and her best friend Liam fake their own holiday romance…but when her fake feelings for Liam start to turn real, Ashley will have to choose what her heart really wants this Christmas.

When egotistical social media influencer DD Ward's dog is shockingly kidnapped, her long-suffering and under-appreciated assistant Emily forms an alliance with a down to earth local veterinarian to find the puppy before Christmas. As the two investigate all possible suspects, the duo form an unbreakable relationship that just might lead them to become more than partners as they find their own puppy love.

Cub reporter Sophia thinks she's found a Christmas story that will save her career when she discovers a long-lost, undelivered Secret Santa gift. Trying to uncover and bring closure to the overdue present before Christmas, Sophia discovers much more than she could have hoped for when she discovers that the gift is not only priceless but stolen.

programmes.t: The Case of the Christmas Diamond
programmes.d: When New York City lawyer Julia Crawley returns to her Rocky Mountain hometown and her family’s lovely inn for the holidays, she finds herself at the center of a generations-old feud with the family that runs the town’s other inn. As the ongoing competition between the two inns escalates, “forbidden” romance blossoms between Julia and Roger Mason, whose family runs the inn that is her family’s big competitor.

Struggling writer Annie Logan is devasted to learn that she won't be able to go home to the family tree farm in time for Christmas due to the demands of her high-powered boss. But when the tree farm is threatened with closure, Annie bids her life in New York goodbye and rushes home to save the place she has always called home.

When Veronika Daniels's co-host leaves "Rise and Shine," she opens auditions for replacements, including Charlie Fisher, a seasoned NY newscaster, and Emily Morgan, a spirited human interest reporter. Emily's unexpected viral plea for the job intensifies the competition. As they vie for the role leading up to the Christmas Day Telethon, old romantic feelings between Charlie and Emily resurface, adding a new layer of complexity to their professional rivalry.
Ex-agent Tae-shik must confront his past when a gang kidnaps a girl he cares for, forcing him into a dangerous mission.

programmes.t: The Tooth and the Nail [English Sub]
programmes.d: In Seoul, a soon after acquiring independence from Japanese occupation, two men met and there came the sound of six shots firing. The police arrests Nam Do-jin, the wealthiest man as a suspect for the murder of a driver named Choi Seung-man. However, all they could find was a burnt body, blood spots, and chopped off fingers. As the trial goes on, it becomes more obvious that the murder had been meticulously planned out and carried out.

Five best swindlers in Korea form a team to rob Korea Bank, the biggest and most difficult bank to rob. Even as they work together for their common goal, each swindler has a secret agenda and does not trust others. After the bank is robbed, the police learn that the anonymous caller who helped them catch some members is a girlfriend of one of the swindlers and that she might be holding the key to solving the mysterious disappearance of money.

Armed with a few clues and an in-depth knowledge of Sherlock Holmes lore, an ice-factory worker (Cris Lankenau) leads his sister and a co-worker on a search for his missing former lover.

Max, Ray and Kai must drag race their crafty foes through the whirlwind, highway-themed dish called the New Jersey Turnpike.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society explore the remnants of a tunnel system once used by an asylum and prison, now known as “Hell’s Tunnel” due to its reported paranormal activity and then, the team embarks on a heartfelt investigation to reach out to the spirit of Prince in Henderson, Minnesota.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society dig into the urban legend of the "Lantern Man" in Le Sueur, Minnesota. Known locally as the "Brewery Hill Spook Light," the figure is rumored to walk the railroad tracks at night with a lantern. Adrian not only confirms the existence of the apparition but also reveals its identity and the reasons it haunts this area.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society investigate a suspected haunting in an old multi-use church. However, the investigation takes an unexpected emotional turn as they connect with a surprising spirit. What begins as a typical haunting becomes deeply personal, and the team moves from assumption to affirmation—all caught on camera.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society venture underground to investigate the caves beneath Jordan Brewery in Jordan, Minnesota. In this unique paranormal investigation, the team encounters a mysterious "non-human" presence and captures stunning visual evidence deep within the caves.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society dive into the urban legend of “Crazy Annie” in Henderson, Minnesota. The chilling tale tells of a grieving woman who drowned her children and hanged herself after her husband died in WWI. The team uncovers how much of this tragic story is rooted in fact and how much is pure fiction.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society investigate the historic Litchfield Opera House in Litchfield, Minnesota. While exploring the location, the team makes contact with two iconic Hollywood performers, Mary Angell and Gale Sondergaard, and captures a full-bodied apparition on thermal camera.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society conduct three investigations across Red Wing, Minnesota, including a stop at what Adrian calls “one of the most haunted locations he’s ever seen” in the basement of Liberty’s Restaurant. They also investigate the Sea Wing disaster memorial and the Red Wing train depot.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society explore the site of a 1933 shootout between the Barrow gang and police near Dexter, Iowa. Though Bonnie and Clyde escaped, the confrontation left Buck Barrow critically wounded and his wife Blanche in police custody. The team investigates lingering spirits from this infamous shootout.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society investigate Green Lawn Cemetery in Southwest Minnesota, a site notorious for teenage “dares” and urban legends. What they uncover is much deeper than anticipated, revealing historical significance alongside paranormal activity.

Adrian Lee and The International Paranormal Society head to Music Row in Nashville, Tennessee for an epic season finale. The investigation spans four iconic locations, starting at the graves of Keith Whitley and Johnny Cash, and ending with an exploration of the Nashville Musicians Association union hall and the world-famous Sound Emporium Studios.
